entries.claim: The widened trust trigger only counts data the design itself writes or changes ("So does a design whose data, anything it writes or changes, shows on a page or service people outside the project can reach"). John's ruling as PLAN-7 records it fires whenever "the design's data shows on a page or service people outside the project can reach". The parenthetical can therefore drop a design that publishes data it only reads.
entries.failure_scenario: Take a body of work under Cadence that adds a read-only public page or feed (browse only, no search box, so no outside input) showing loan or member records the already-built code writes. The design writes and changes nothing that shows there, so under the literal text neither the outside-input trigger nor the new reach trigger fires. The spine step never asks "What can people outside the project send in, and what must they never see or change?" for the one part whose job is showing data to outsiders, and no decision records what they must never see. Expectation source: the ruling's wording in PLAN-7.md line 36. Whether read-only exposure should count is a ruling call, not something the repo settles.

entries.claim: plainStringProblems only checks the line that holds the key, so an unquoted plain description that wraps onto an indented continuation line holding ": " passes the test. That is the class the test claims (an unquoted plain value containing ": "), and YAML rejects or misreads it.
entries.failure_scenario: Demonstrated with PyYAML 6.0.3 and the test's own regexes. Input 1: 'description: Resumes a session whose answer is quoted\n  word for word: the trust answer lands in the spine.' plainStringProblems returns [], and yaml.safe_load raises ScannerError "mapping values are not allowed here", so the case can't load (900d872's failure). Input 2: 'description:\n  Resumes a session, word for word: the trust answer.' This also returns [], and YAML reads description as a mapping {'Resumes a session, word for word': 'the trust answer.'}, not a string. No case.yaml in the tree wraps today (all 56 descriptions are single-line), so the gap is latent.
